newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat says Satelindo sale later this year.
newsitem.headline: Indosat says Satelindo sale later this year.

text.p: Indonesia's telecommunications firm PT Indonesian Satellite Corporation (Indosat) said on Tuesday it expected to complete the proposed sale of most of its 7.5 percent stake in PT Satelit Palapa Indonesia (Satelindo) later this year.

"The negotiations are still going on, but we expect the sale to be completed later this year. The sale could have a positive impact on the firm's this year results if it is completed before year-end," investor relations manager Budi Prasetyo told Reuters.
New York-listed Indosat said in April it planned to sell a 6.5 percent stake in telecommunications firm Satelindo out of its total holding of 7.5 percent.
Satelindo's shareholders include PT Bimagraha Telekomindo controlled by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmojo, Deutsche Telkom's DeTeMobil and state-controlled PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia.
Satelindo's business interests included international telephone and cellular telephone services.
Prasetyo declined to give further details, but said the firm planned to hold a news conference on Wednesday to announce its financial results for the first six months of 1997.
Laksono Widodo, an analyst with ING Baring Securities Indonesia, said he expected the firm to post an encouraging first half net profit partly due to the rupiah depreciation against the U.S. dollar.
"The results are likely to be encouraging partly because of the rupiah's depreciation against the dollar," Widodo said, adding that Indosat remained largely an importer of international traffic.
Widodo said Indosat was expected to post a net profit of 596 billion rupiah in 1997 against 523.5 billion rupiah in 1996.
